highlights: The market recovered on 19 Nov: the ASPI rose 140 points (+0.66%) to 21,543.12 and the S&P SL20 rose 0.75% to 6,142.43, on thin turnover of Rs 1.73bn. Banks, LOLC-group financials and capital goods gained; SLT-Mobitel rose 4.94% and Ceylon Tea Services 10.95%, while Dialog was flat.
Foreigners were net sellers of Rs 95.85M ($287.9K): bought Rs 39M, sold Rs 135M. Almost all the selling was in Dialog (≈Rs 101M) and Hemas (≈Rs 23M); the buying was led by HNB (≈Rs 21M).

Big disagreement on Access Engineering (AEL.N0000): HNB Stockbrokers cut it to Hold from Moderate buy with a Rs 90 target (price Rs 82.90), while this site's fair value is Rs 47 (buy below Rs 40). The broker says 2Q FY27 profit to shareholders rose 158% to Rs 4.1bn, but mostly on Marina Square apartment handovers and a one-off tax credit; without the apartments, revenue fell about 7%.

Banks became much more cautious about lending in 3Q even as loan demand rose, a Central Bank survey showed, ahead of Friday's (20 Nov) monetary policy announcement. Fitch backed Budget 2027 as consistent with fiscal discipline.
Customs had collected Rs 2,456.8bn by 16 Nov, already above its full-year target of Rs 2,207bn, and Colombo Port transshipment volumes rose 10% in the first ten months of 2026.

news.title: Banks' willingness to lend cools: CBSL survey
news.text: The Central Bank's credit supply survey showed banks' overall willingness to lend slowing to 27.4 in 3Q from 40.4 in 2Q, across retail, corporate and SME lending, while loan demand picked up. Banks expect the gap to widen in 4Q. The monetary policy decision is due on Friday 20 Nov.

news.title: Customs already above its 2026 revenue target
news.text: Sri Lanka Customs collected Rs 2,456.8bn by 16 November against a full-year target of Rs 2,207bn, and has beaten its monthly target for ten months running. Collections in the first half of November were over 59% of the month's target.

news.title: Colombo Port transshipment up 10%
news.text: Transshipment volumes rose to about 6.41mn TEUs in January–October 2026 from about 5.83mn a year earlier. Colombo rose to 20th among the world's busiest container ports in the first half (Alphaliner), from 26th at the end of 2025.

news.title: SLT-Mobitel: profit up 59%, staff pay costs stay
news.text: SLT-Mobitel's 9-month group profit after tax rose 59.4% to Rs 10.03bn on 11.1% revenue growth. The chair said the company will keep paying the recently matched salaries, costing a 'few billion' rupees a year.

news.title: Fitch backs Budget 2027
news.text: Fitch said Budget 2027 shows continued commitment to fiscal discipline and debt reduction while allowing more spending on investment and cyclone rebuilding. It upgraded Sri Lanka to B-/Stable from CCC+ in September.

news.title: Global: Anthropic IPO; Trump meets Xi and Putin
news.text: Anthropic raised $81bn in the largest IPO on record, upsized to 980mn shares, plus a $26bn private placement, valuing it at about $1.5tn fully diluted. US President Trump was to end his Asia trip with a meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin focused on nuclear arms control. On 18 Nov the Dow fell 1.11% and the S&P 500 0.23%; Taiwan's TAIEX fell 3.67% on the morning screen.

keyPoints: Revenue +36% to Rs 20.4bn, but Rs 6.4bn (32%) came from Marina Square apartment handovers; without them revenue fell about 7%.
Vehicles −10% as pent-up demand fades; construction materials −26% after the West Container Terminal job ended; civil engineering only +7.3%, a slow order book.

Profit to shareholders +158% to Rs 4.1bn (EPS Rs 4.08), helped by a Rs 735mn one-off tax credit; about +130% without it. Net finance cost doubled as apartment borrowing costs are no longer capitalised.
Net debt flat at Rs 39.5bn; a Rs 3.1bn working-capital outflow, capex and dividends used up the operating cash.
Cut to Hold: about 9% upside to the Rs 90 target; short-term outlook Neutral. The P/E is near its historical average; ROE above its average.
forecasts: FY27E EPS Rs 12.33 (profit Rs 12.3bn); FY28E EPS Rs 13.34
First-half EPS of about Rs 5.35 (excluding the one-off) is only 43% of the FY27E forecast, so the year depends on the second half
Apartment revenue must nearly double in the second half; net finance costs are already about 73% of the full-year estimate
Technicals: above its 50- and 200-day averages but momentum fading (RSI 64); needs to hold about Rs 80
risks: A long bitumen shortage could delay road works and slow order book conversion
High debt could keep finance costs up
Delays in Marina Square handovers could hurt second-half earnings
catalysts: Two Ruwanpura Expressway Phase I packages worth about Rs 45.6bn
Year-end government capex, and a 2027 capex budget about 40% higher at Rs 2.0tn
Radiopharmaceutical revenue growing as operations ramp up
